nodes.description: A patent document titled "Computer system to visualize data from an IP rights database" describing a system for visualizing IP rights data as a geographic map.

A computer system (10) that visualizes data from an IP rights database as a geographic map with a viewable area, comprising a map display change monitor, an IP rights list generator, and an information display generator.<SEP>A system with one or more processors and memory configured to evaluate information via a computer network, performing keyword identification, weight determination, ranking, and advertisement selection.<SEP>A computer-based system that detects user interest, identifies keywords, determines keyword weights, receives content requests, ranks keywords, and selects content such as advertisements for display with information resources.

A database containing IP rights records, including geographic addresses of IP right owners, from which lists of IP rights are generated and restricted.<SEP>A database containing intellectual property rights records, including geographic addresses of IP right owners, used as the source for generating lists of IP rights.
A displayed geographic map having a viewable area whose geographic coordinates define the geographic area used to filter IP rights by owner address.

A component (23) that receives and stores geographic coordinates of the viewable area, compares current coordinates with previously stored coordinates, and generates a display change notification, including after a pre-defined time period elapses with no change.

A notification generated by the map display change monitor that includes the geographic coordinates of the current viewable area of the geographic map.<SEP>A notification issued upon detecting a change in the viewable area of the geographic map, generated after a pre-defined time period elapses with no change in the viewable area.

A component (37) that generates a list of IP rights from the IP rights database whose owner's geographic address falls within the current viewable area, and restricts the list based on restriction criteria to form a restricted list.
An interface that ascertains one or more restriction criteria related to the IP rights used to restrict the generated list of IP rights.

Criteria related to IP rights used to restrict the list of IP rights, including IP jurisdiction, type of IP right, technology type, industry type, filing date, number of applications filed by the owner, owner being an individual or corporation, representative listing, IPC classes, and trademark classes.<SEP>Criteria related to IP rights used to restrict a list of IP rights, including IP jurisdiction, type of IP right, technology type, industry type, filing date, number of applications, owner type, representative listing, IPC classes, and trademark classes.

A list of IP rights filtered to those whose owner address is within the current viewable area and further restricted based on one or more restriction criteria.<SEP>A list of IP rights filtered from the IP rights database based on one or more restriction criteria related to the IP rights.

A component (26) that generates and displays an information pane containing data visualizations derived from the restricted list of IP rights and updates them upon each successive display change notification.<SEP>A component that generates and displays an information pane containing data visualizations derived from a restricted list of IP rights, updating them based on geographic coordinates of the current viewable map area.

A displayed pane containing one or more data visualizations derived from the restricted list of IP rights.<SEP>A display area containing one or more data visualizations related to the restricted list of IP rights.

Visualizations derived from the restricted list of IP rights, including technology type charts, industry type charts, filing trend analysis charts, and IP rights owner filing size charts.<SEP>Visual representations generated in the information pane related to the restricted list of IP rights, such as technology type charts, industry type charts, filing trend analysis charts, owner filing size charts, and lists of IP rights owners.
A component that allows the user to select one or more data visualizations based on the restriction criteria.
An interface that displays a geographic map having a viewable area.
A history of use of the system provided by storing geographic coordinates of the viewable area for an entire session or multiple sessions.

An owner of an IP right whose geographic address is used to determine whether the IP right falls within the geographic area of the current viewable area.<SEP>An individual or corporation that owns an IP right, whose geographic address is used to determine whether the IP right falls within the current viewable map area.
A map interface displaying a viewable geographic area whose coordinates are used to define the geographic area for filtering IP rights by owner address.
A message generated in relation to a change in the viewable area of the geographic map, generated after a pre-defined time period elapses and there has been no change in the viewable area.
Coordinates defining the current viewable area of the geographic map display, used to define the geographic area for filtering IP rights and to update data visualizations.

A process for visualizing data from an IP rights database involving receiving map change messages, obtaining geographic coordinates, generating and restricting lists of IP rights, and generating and updating data visualizations.
Restriction criteria that a user can select to restrict the list of IP rights.
A default configuration of one or more restriction criteria applied to restrict the list of IP rights.
Data visualizations that a user can select, based on the restriction criteria.
A default configuration of data visualizations based on a default setting of the restriction criteria.
A button displayed on screen that a user can press to initiate a command to generate or update data visualizations.
A command initiated by a user, such as pressing an on-screen button, that triggers generating or updating data visualizations.
Defined International Patent Classification classes used as a restriction criterion for patent IP rights.
Defined classes used as a restriction criterion for trademark IP rights.
A data visualization chart showing filing trend analysis for the IP rights.

A patent publication titled "Methods and apparatus of context-data acquisition and ranking" that discloses a system, method, and article of manufacture for acquiring and ranking context data based on a query derived from a short message.
A method of determining a context-data type from a query, identifying context-data sources, generating requests for context data, and ranking received context data according to a specified parameter.
A classification of context data determined algorithmically from the meaning of a term of a short message, providing information about the environment or context of a mobile device.
A provider that supplies context data of a particular context-data type and can be ranked according to a specified parameter such as pecuniary cost.

A message whose content has a meaning to which context-data is related, and to which relevant context-data is linked and formatted according to a communication protocol.<SEP>A message received from a mobile device by a server, whose term meanings are used to determine a context-data type and to which received context data may be appended or encoded.

A device that generates a short message and a query, and to which received context data may be provided; may be a smart phone.<SEP>A device that includes at least a camera and a screen, runs an application in operative communication with the camera, and displays results by augmenting the source image with indicia. It may be a mobile phone, tablet, PDA, or dedicated camera.<SEP>A device including at least a camera and a screen, running an application that communicates with the search service via an Internet access mechanism; may be a mobile phone, tablet, PDA, or dedicated camera.

A computing device used by a context-data provider to collect a set of context-data.<SEP>A computing system that receives short messages from mobile devices, determines context-data types, identifies and ranks context-data sources, and generates requests for context data.<SEP>A computing system that receives requests, traverses social networks to identify connecting persons, and sends identifiers or responses back to the requesting person's computer.<SEP>A server hosted by the computing device that performs the typographical error classification operations.<SEP>A computing system that streams video content features to a client.<SEP>A server that receives data comprising characteristics of e-mail exchanges from the interaction database, assigns weights to characteristics, and transfers data to a processor.<SEP>A server that receives data comprising characteristics of e-mail exchanges, assigns weights to characteristics, and transfers data to a processor for generating relationship data.
A mobile device that receives context data, short messages with appended context data, or a Uniform Resource Identifier of a database server.

A criterion used to rank context-data sources, comprising a pecuniary cost to acquire context data, a state of the receiving mobile device, a state of an available communication network, or a cost value of the context data.
A monetary cost to acquire context data from a context-data source, used as a specified parameter for ranking context-data sources.

A storage system available to a recipient mobile device in which received context data may be stored and queried via metadata instructions.<SEP>A storage that holds keywords and their weights, associating increased keyword weights with the parked domain web page having the unique identifier.<SEP>A storage system from which keywords of advertisements are identified using the unique identifier of the parked domain web page, and in which increased keyword weights are associated with the parked domain web page.<SEP>A database in which management data is stored in a searchable format.<SEP>A storage repository in which extracted management data is stored in a searchable format for subsequent review and query by users and administrators.<SEP>A searchable-format store in which the management data is stored.<SEP>A searchable storage system in which management data is stored in a searchable format.
An identifier of a database server that may be forwarded to a receiving mobile device to access stored context data.
A language used to encode received context data into a short message.
An apparatus comprising at least one memory with program instructions and at least one processor configured to execute operations for context-data acquisition and ranking.
A medium comprising computer-executable instructions adapted to perform the context-data acquisition and ranking method.
A device by which context-data is obtained.<SEP>A sensor by which context data related to the meaning of short message content is obtained.

An entity with at least one server that collects and provides a set of context-data related to the meaning of short message content, and is allowed to provide a cost of the context-data.<SEP>A provider from which a set of context data related to the meaning of short message content is collected by a server.

A measure used to algorithmically select relevant context-data, comprising a monetary cost of the context-data.<SEP>A measure according to which relevant context data is algorithmically selected, comprising a monetary cost of the context data.
A type of mobile device that may generate the short message whose term meanings determine the context-data type.
Data elements related to the meaning or physical context of a short message, collected from context-data providers and weighted or selected according to at least one metric such as monetary cost.
The cost of context-data, used as a metric for algorithmically selecting relevant context-data.
A protocol according to which relevant context-data and the short message are formatted, such as a cellular network short message protocol or an internet communication protocol.
A type of communication protocol used for formatting the relevant context-data and the short message.
A type of communication protocol used for formatting the relevant context-data and the short message.
A device that generated the short message and has a physical context to which the context-data is related.
A patent (US9514753B2) describing methods, systems, and apparatus for performing speaker identification using hash-based indexing of speaker vectors.

A vector derived from an utterance, used as a query to compare against speaker vectors.<SEP>A vector derived from an utterance, used as the query representation in speaker identification; may be an i-vector or based on deep neural network activations.

A vector derived from one or more utterances of a respective speaker, used to represent characteristics of that speaker's speech.<SEP>A vector derived from one or more utterances of a respective speaker, stored in hash tables and compared against an utterance vector to identify a speaker.
Values determined for an utterance vector or speaker vector according to multiple different hash functions, used to look up speaker vectors in hash tables.
Multiple different functions used to compute hash values; may include locality sensitive hash functions or functions based on positions of vectors with respect to hyperplanes.
A plurality of tables storing speaker vectors indexed by hash values, from which a set of speaker vectors is determined.
Speech input from which an utterance vector is derived and whose speaker is to be identified.

A person whose speech characteristics are represented by speaker vectors and who is associated with a speaker identity.<SEP>A person whose speech characteristics are represented by speaker vectors and whose identity is determined from the selected speaker vector.

The identity of a speaker determined based on associations between speaker vectors and respective speakers, corresponding to a selected speaker vector.<SEP>The identity of a speaker determined from the selected speaker vector and output as data.
A vector comprising parameters determined using multivariate factor analysis of an utterance or of one or more utterances of a speaker.
A neural network whose activations, occurring in response to information about an utterance, are used to determine parameters of utterance and speaker vectors.
A type of hash function used to determine hash values for vectors in the speaker identification method.
Geometric constructs with respect to which the position of an utterance vector is used to determine hash values.
Scores indicating the degree of similarity between the utterance vector and each speaker vector in the set, used to select the most similar speaker vector.
A measure of distance between the utterance vector and each speaker vector in the set, used to determine similarity scores.
A threshold against which the smallest cosine distance is compared to decide whether to select the corresponding speaker vector.
Items that include utterances of a speaker corresponding to the selected speaker vector and may be identified and output.
A set of multiple video resources accessed to generate speaker vectors for speakers.
A process of authenticating a particular user based on determining that the selected speaker vector corresponds to that user.
An utterance vector comprising parameters determined using multivariate factor analysis of the utterance.
A speaker vector comprising parameters determined using multivariate factor analysis of one or more utterances of a respective speaker.
A data structure from which speaker vectors are determined using hash values.
A value determined for an utterance vector according to a hash function, used to look up speaker vectors in hash tables.
A function used to determine hash values for an utterance vector, with multiple different hash functions being applied.
A video resource for which a speaker vector is generated, with a set of multiple video resources being accessed.
A technique used to determine parameters of utterance i-vectors and speaker i-vectors.

A device storing instructions that, when executed by one or more computers, cause the computers to perform operations for speaker identification.<SEP>A storage device with an executable program stored thereon that instructs a processor to perform the filtration method.<SEP>A storage device containing an executable program for presenting digital media content, establishing user relationships, and determining relevancy weights, as described in the claims.
A computing device that executes stored instructions to perform operations.

A patent publication titled "Systems and methods for selecting content using weighted terms," describing techniques for evaluating information via a computer network using weighted keywords to select content for display.

A web page with a unique identifier that lacks content having keywords other than content provided via the data processing system; it displays advertisements and serves as the context for keyword weighting and advertisement selection.<SEP>A web page with a unique identifier that lacks content having keywords other than content provided via the data processing system, used as the information resource on which advertisements are displayed and evaluated.<SEP>A web page associated with a parked domain on which advertisements and keywords are displayed; keyword weights are specific to this page.

A term associated with an advertisement displayed on a parked domain web page; keywords have weights determined by user interest and historic performance, and are ranked to select advertisements.<SEP>A term associated with subject matter of an information resource or advertisement, assigned a weight per information resource and used to select content for display.<SEP>Keywords of data files of a data-stream, obtained by indexing types of data, included in the management data.

A numerical value assigned to a keyword, increased by adding a point in response to user interest, and determined based on user interest and historic performance; used to rank keywords.<SEP>A value determined for each keyword for a given information resource, based on user interest indications and historic performance, used to rank keywords and select content.<SEP>A weight assigned to each of a plurality of characteristics for each pair of users, used in determining relationship strength.

An ad displayed with a parked domain web page, associated with one or more keywords; advertisements are selected for display based on the highest ranked keyword.<SEP>Content displayed on a web page, associated with one or more keywords, whose user interest indications inform keyword weighting and which is selected for display based on ranked keywords.

An advertisement displayed with the parked domain web page, associated with the first keyword, in which the first user indicated interest.<SEP>An advertisement displayed on the parked domain web page, associated with a first keyword, whose user interest indications from a first user inform the weight of the first keyword.<SEP>An advertisement referenced in the context of the parked domain web page, distinct from the second advertisement and the third advertisement.

An advertisement displayed on the parked domain web page, associated with the second keyword, in which the second user indicated interest.<SEP>An advertisement displayed on the parked domain web page, associated with a second keyword, whose user interest indications from a second user inform the weight of the second keyword.<SEP>An advertisement displayed on the parked domain web page, associated with the second keyword, in which the second user indicates interest.

An advertisement different from the first and second advertisements, selected for display with the parked domain web page based at least in part on the first keyword selected as the highest ranked keyword.<SEP>An advertisement different from the first and second advertisements, selected for display with the parked domain web page based on the first keyword ranked as the highest ranked keyword.<SEP>An advertisement selected to provide for display with the parked domain web page based at least in part on the first keyword selected as the highest ranked keyword; it is different from the first advertisement and the second advertisement.

An advertisement of the parked domain web page associated with the third keyword, in which user interest may be indicated.<SEP>An advertisement displayed on the parked domain web page associated with the first keyword, for which an indication of user interest may be received.

A user whose indication of interest in a first advertisement displayed on the parked domain web page is received.<SEP>A user whose indication of interest in the first advertisement displayed on the parked domain web page is received and used to determine keyword weights.<SEP>A user referenced in the context of the parked domain web page, distinct from the second user and the third user.<SEP>The user seeking assistance in finding a second user through a social network; has an identifier, a location, and a social network that may be traversed and combined from multiple social network types.

A user whose indication of interest in a second advertisement displayed on the parked domain web page is received.<SEP>A user whose indication of interest in the second advertisement displayed on the parked domain web page is received and used to determine the second keyword's weight.<SEP>A user whose indication of user interest in the second advertisement displayed on the parked domain web page is received.<SEP>The user whom the first user is trying to find; has an associated identifier and a social network.

A user different from the first and second users who requests content to provide for display with the parked domain web page.<SEP>A user different from the first user and the second user who requests content to provide for display with the parked domain web page.<SEP>A user in the social network of the first user who is likely to connect the first user's social network with the third user's own social network and who has a last-known location within a predetermined distance from the first user's location; may opt in to sharing identity, social network, or location information.
A signal of a user's interest in an advertisement, including at least one of a click, a selection, a finger gesture, a mouse over, and a conversion.
A form of user interest indication in which a user clicks on an advertisement displayed on the parked domain web page.
A form of user interest indication representing a completed desired action by a user in response to an advertisement.

Past performance on the parked domain web page of keywords corresponding to user interest of users other than the first user, used in determining keyword weights.<SEP>Past performance data of keywords on the parked domain web page corresponding to user interest of users other than the first user, used in determining keyword weights.

An identifier of a parked domain web page used to identify keywords associated with an advertisement and to associate increased keyword weights with the page.<SEP>An identifier of the parked domain web page used to identify a plurality of keywords of the first advertisement from a database.
A request received from a user for content to provide for display with the parked domain web page, triggering keyword ranking and content selection.
The process of ordering keywords based on their weights to select a highest ranked keyword for content selection.
The process of choosing content, such as an advertisement, to provide for display with an information resource based at least in part on a selected keyword or its associated weight.
Interactions of users with advertisements previously displayed on the parked domain web page, whose number is used to assign weights to keywords.

An attribute associated with user interest in an advertisement, including at least one of a temporal characteristic, a day characteristic, a web page content slot characteristic, a monetary characteristic, and a performance characteristic, used in determining keyword weights.<SEP>A characteristic of e-mail exchanges between pairs of users, such as interaction frequency, interaction type, number of communication participants, time between interactions, time since a first interaction, time since a last interaction, interaction volume, and a ratio of source to target versus target to source interactions.
A network via which the system evaluates information.<SEP>A network via which the data processing system receives user interest indications and requests for content.

A keyword of the plurality of keywords having a first weight on the parked domain web page and a different weight on a second information resource; it can be ranked highest and selected to choose a third advertisement.<SEP>A keyword of a plurality of keywords having a first weight on the parked domain web page and a different weight on a second information resource; it is ranked against other keywords and may be selected as the highest ranked keyword.

A keyword of the plurality of keywords associated with a second advertisement, having a second weight determined based on the second user's interest.<SEP>A keyword of the plurality of keywords associated with a second advertisement displayed on the parked domain web page; its second weight is determined based on an indication of user interest.
A keyword of the plurality of keywords associated with a third advertisement, having a third weight determined based on user interest.

An information resource on which the first keyword has a different weight than on the parked domain web page.<SEP>An information resource on which the first keyword has a weight different from its first weight on the parked domain web page.
A weight value that the weight of the highest weighted keyword must satisfy when selecting the highest weighted keyword.

A medium having instructions to evaluate information, comprising instructions to perform keyword identification, weight determination, ranking, and advertisement selection.<SEP>A computer readable medium storing instructions, referenced in claim 18 and claim 19.<SEP>A medium containing executable instructions that when executed perform a method of generating relationship data.<SEP>A medium containing executable instructions that when executed perform a method of modeling relationships between e-mail users.
The weight of the first keyword on the parked domain web page, used in ranking the first keyword against the second keyword.
The weight of the second keyword, determined based on the indication of user interest of the second user in the second advertisement.
A signal indicating a user's interest in an advertisement displayed on the parked domain web page, used to determine a keyword weight.
A request from the third user for content to provide for display with the parked domain web page.
The first keyword is selected as the highest ranked keyword based on ranking higher than the second keyword.

A patent document titled "Finding people using social networks" that describes embodiments for assisting a first person in finding a second person using a social network, including systems, methods, and privacy mechanisms.
A person who sends a request to a server identifying himself or herself, the person being sought, and the requestor's location, in order to find a target person using a social network.
The second person whom the requesting person is trying to find through the social network.

A person in the social network of the requesting person who is likely to connect the requesting person's social network with the target person's social network and who has a last-known location within a predetermined distance from the requesting person's location.

A network of relationships among people, comprising information from at least one social network service, used to connect a requesting person with a target person.<SEP>A network of users associated with the first user, which may be determined based on the first user's identifier, may combine different types of social networks, and may be traversed and pruned based on locations of people in the network.
A service that provides social network information used to determine a person's social network.
Mechanisms disclosed in the patent for protecting user privacy, including anonymizing identifying information and encrypting communications.

A consent by a connecting person to share information about his or her identity, social network, or location with people of at least as many degrees of separation as the number of degrees of separation for the type of relationship involved.
A measure of the number of intermediary connections between two people in a social network, used to determine opt-in sharing eligibility.
A classification of the relationship between the requesting person and the connecting person, associated with a number of degrees of separation for opt-in purposes.
The most recent location determined for a connecting person, based on a wireless network, geolocation, a venue, or an event the person identified himself or herself as being at.

A threshold distance from the requesting person's location within which a connecting person's last-known location must fall.<SEP>A distance threshold from the location of the first user within which the third user's last-known location must fall.

An additional person in the social network of the requesting person who is likely to connect the requesting person's social network with the target person's social network, whose response may be combined or prioritized with the connecting person's response.
A network to which a connecting person's computer is connected, used to determine the last-known location of the connecting person.
Location information provided by a connecting person's computer, used to determine the last-known location of the connecting person.

A place that a connecting person has identified himself or herself as being at, used to determine the last-known location.<SEP>A place that the third user has identified himself or herself as being at, or that may be the same as the last-known location of the third user and the location of the first user.

An occurrence that a connecting person has identified himself or herself as being at, used to determine the last-known location.<SEP>An occurrence that the third user has identified himself or herself as being at, or that may be the same as the last-known location of the third user and the location of the first user.<SEP>A condition registered for monitoring with regard to a history object, triggered when stored information describing ETL process performance satisfies specified criteria, causing a subscribed ETL process to be performed.<SEP>An occurrence registered for monitoring with regard to a history object, triggered when the performance of an ETL process satisfies criteria, causing a subscribed ETL process to be performed.
A privacy mechanism that removes or obscures identifying information about users.
A privacy mechanism that encrypts communications between parties to protect user information.
A unified format to which responses from multiple connecting persons' computers are converted so they can be combined.

A user whose identifier may be withheld from the first user based on a negative affinity with the first user or because the time associated with the fourth user's last-known location is older than a threshold; may connect the first and third users.
A device having a pre-determined location at which the identifier associated with the first user may be received.

A storage medium bearing computer-executable instructions that, when executed on a computer, cause the computer to perform operations for assisting a first user in finding a second user using a social network.
A replacement value used to anonymize results by replacing an identifier associated with the second user.
A location of the first user that may be a geographic location, used in determining the third user within a predetermined distance.

The number of degrees of separation between the first user and the third user, associated with a type of relationship, used to determine whether the third user has opted in to sharing information with users of at least as many degrees of separation.
The type of relationship between the first user and the third user, associated with a number of degrees of separation.
A negative relationship between the first user and a fourth user that may cause a determination not to return the fourth user's identifier.
A time limit used to determine whether to withhold sending an identifier associated with a fourth user based on the age of the fourth user's last-known location.
Results produced by replacing an identifier associated with the second user with a token and encrypting the results.
An identifier associated with a user (first, second, third, or fourth), which may include a name, image, or location, and may be replaced with a token or withheld.
A patented method and system (US8095432B1) for generating ranked recommendation lists for items based on relationship proximity between members of a social networking utility.

A social network platform in which members have relationships such as friends, non-friends, and group members, and within which recommendations for items are obtained, ranked, and searched.<SEP>A social network platform within which members are connected as friends or non-friends and in which items can be searched and recommended.

A member of the social networking utility who requests searches for items, receives recommendation lists, and whose network and interests define relationship proximity for ranking recommendations.<SEP>A member of the social networking utility who requests a search for an item and receives a generated recommendation list.

A member of the social networking utility who is a friend of the inquiring member and provides a first recommendation for an item, sharing a plurality of interests in common with the inquiring member.<SEP>A member of the social networking utility who is a friend of the inquiring member and who provides a first recommendation for the item.

A member of the social networking utility who is a non-friend of the inquiring member and who provides a second recommendation for the item.<SEP>A member of the social networking utility who is a non-friend of the inquiring member and provides a second recommendation for the item.

A member of the social networking utility who has a plurality of different interests than the inquiring member and who provides a third recommendation for the item.<SEP>A member of the social networking utility who has a plurality of different interests than the inquiring member and provides a third recommendation for the item.

An opinion or endorsement of an item provided by a member of the social networking utility, which is ranked and displayed based on relationship proximity.<SEP>A recommendation for presentation of the second network content sent to a user.
A product or object that is recommended, searched for, ranked, and potentially purchased within the social networking utility.
A measure of closeness between members within the social networking utility, closest for friends and farthest for strangers, used to rank recommendations.

A generated list of recommendations for the item, ordered so that the first recommendation is higher than the second recommendation based on the first rank exceeding the second rank.<SEP>An ordered list of recommendations for an item generated by the processor, with higher-ranked recommendations placed above lower-ranked ones.

The term "Processor" refers to a hardware component or processing unit that executes software programs and performs a wide range of computational operations across various systems and methods. As a component coupled to memory and programmed by program code stored in the memory, the processor implements the modules of an apparatus and is capable of carrying out actions such as receiving, extracting, and storing management data. It is operable to execute a software program that performs steps for receiving a data-stream, extracting management data, and storing the management data in a searchable format.

In the context of recommendation systems, the processor is a hardware component used to determine relationship proximities, rank recommendations, and generate recommendation lists, as well as to execute the recommendation application and perform the operations of the system. It also performs the steps of establishing user relationships and other related method operations.

Additionally, the processor serves as a processing unit used to perform clustering and inventory estimation steps in a given method and system. As a component of a network device, it is operative to perform first pass analysis, second pass analysis, misclassification display, and purging actions.<SEP>A processor that generates relationship data by determining a relationship strength associated with each pair of users.<SEP>A component in communication with the memory that executes the stored instructions.

A storage component operatively connected to the processor in which the recommendation application resides.<SEP>A storage component operatively connected to the processor and holding the recommendation application.<SEP>A component of an apparatus operatively coupled to a processing device.<SEP>Memory coupled to the processor that stores program code programming the processor.<SEP>A component that stores instructions for receiving queries, embedding cases, providing query types, and returning subsets of cases or experts.

A software application executing on a processor and resident in memory, configured to obtain recommendations for an item from members of a social networking utility, determine relationship proximities, rank recommendations, perform searches, and generate a recommendation list.<SEP>A software application executing on the processor and resident in memory, configured to obtain recommendations, rank them, and generate recommendation lists.
A system from which inventory details associated with an item are received.
A group associated with an item to which the inquiring member may be added.
A feed of the inquiring member that is updated to include a reduced price and the original price of an item.
Tags generated for an item and associated with the item to enable searching.
Details associated with an item that are received and associated with recommendations.
Reports generated for an item.
A transaction performed for the item in response to a received request to purchase the item.<SEP>A transaction performed for an item upon receiving a request to purchase the item.

The set of members connected to the inquiring member within the social networking utility, containing friends and excluding non-friends.<SEP>A network comprising a diagnosis assistance system and a set of user devices linking requesters and experts with the system.
Members of a group of the inquiring member whose relationship proximity is closer than that of non-group members.
Members who are not in a group of the inquiring member and whose relationship proximity is farther than that of group members.

A plurality of items identified as favorites of the inquiring member, which can be shared with a network of the inquiring member.<SEP>Items identified as favorites of the inquiring member that may be shared with the inquiring member's network.
A recommendation for the item obtained from the first member, ranked with a first rank based on the first relationship proximity.
A recommendation for the item obtained from the second member, ranked with a second rank based on the second relationship proximity.
A recommendation for the item provided by the third member, ranked with a third rank.
A measure of the relationship proximity between the first member and the inquiring member, used to rank the first recommendation.
A measure of the relationship proximity between the second member and the inquiring member, used to rank the second recommendation.
The rank assigned to the first recommendation, which exceeds the second rank and the third rank.
The rank assigned to the second recommendation, which is lower than the first rank.
The rank assigned to the third recommendation, which is lower than the first rank.
A request received from the inquiring member to search for the item in the social networking utility.
An external social network platform from which the recommendation application is configured to obtain a plurality of recommendations.
An application with which the recommendation application is configured to interact.
An application with which the recommendation application is configured to interact.
A storage medium storing instructions that provide functionality to generate a recommendation list for an item.
The search for the item may be filtered by the network of the inquiring member.

The title of the patent US8880423B2, referring to techniques for estimating advertisement inventory for search retargeting segments.

The term "User" refers to an individual interacting with various digital systems and content platforms, encompassing several distinct roles and capabilities. In the context of search and inventory systems, a User is someone who has previously submitted search keywords and viewed pages, thereby providing the history used for inventory estimation. In a feedback and editing context, a User is a person who provides feedback on a work, including marking potential typographical errors as author-intended strings.

Regarding messaging systems, a User is a person for whom messages are sorted into folders and who is presented with a list of possibly misclassified messages, enabling them to move identified messages to another folder. Such a User is also enabled to move an identified message to another message folder and can select execution of a multi-pass message filter through an interface on the client device.

In the realm of content interaction and recommendation, a User is a person who interacts with video content features and is associated with a preferred character based on interaction data, receiving content recommendations as a result. Similarly, a User is a person who interacts with network content and expresses preferences toward characters, and may provide explicit feedback favoring a first fictional character via a user interface. More broadly, a User is an individual who has online associations with content producers and receives filtered, prioritized digital media content. US9589231B2 is the publication number of the patent titled "Social Medical Network for Diagnosis Assistance".
edges.target: Social Medical Network For Diagnosis Assistance

edges.description: The patent US9589231B2 describes a method for diagnosis assistance exploiting similarity between new medical cases and existing cases and experts.
The diagnosis assistance method embeds a new medical case in an embedding space in which existing medical cases and experts are embedded.
The method receives a query request including a new medical case from a requester.
The method provides for the requester to select a query-for-cases among a plurality of query types.
The method provides for the requester to select a query-for-experts among a plurality of query types.
The system comprises memory storing instructions for performing the diagnosis assistance method and a processor for executing the instructions.
The computer program product stores instructions that when executed on a computer cause the computer to perform the diagnosis assistance method.
The new medical case is embedded in the embedding space alongside existing cases and experts.
The set of existing medical cases is embedded in the embedding space.
The set of experts is embedded in the embedding space.
Multidimensional representations of existing cases, experts, and the new case are generated in the embedding space.
The embedding of the new medical case in the embedding space comprises computing a multidimensional representation of the medical case based on a medical ontology.
The new medical case comprises a plurality of records relating to a specific patient.
The requester submits a query request that includes a new medical case.

When query-for-cases is selected, a subset of existing cases is returned based on computed similarity between the embedded new case and embedded existing cases.<SEP>When the query-for-cases is selected, a subset of the existing medical cases is returned based on computed similarity between the embedded new case and the embedded existing cases.
edges.keywords: returns subset,returns subset based on similarity,similarity

edges.description: When query-for-experts is selected, a subset of experts is returned based on computed similarity between the embedded new case and embedded experts.<SEP>When the query-for-experts is selected, a subset of the experts is returned based on computed similarity between the embedded new case and the embedded experts.
edges.keywords: returns subset,returns subset based on similarity,similarity

edges.description: Experts are each embedded based on information including a profile of the expert.
Experts are each embedded based on coded medical procedures which have been performed by the expert.
Experts are each embedded based on articles authored by the expert.
Experts are each embedded based on stored medical cases linked to the expert.

edges.description: The user devices link experts with the diagnosis assistance system.
The new case is communicated to one of the subset of experts for the expert to attempt to provide a diagnosis.
The requester is provided the ability to select from a plurality of query types.
The user devices link requesters with the diagnosis assistance system.

A cost is computed for the query, with the cost for a query-for-cases differing from the cost for a query-for-experts.<SEP>The computed query cost is lower for a query-for-cases than for a query-for-experts.
When the query-for-cases is selected, documents from a public database are returned based on computed similarity between the embedded new case and embedded documents.

The query-by-experts has a second cost higher than the first cost of query-by-cases.<SEP>When the query-by-cases is selected, provision is made for a query-by-experts to be performed subsequent to the query-by-cases.

A cost is computed for the query, with the cost for a query-for-experts differing from the cost for a query-for-cases.<SEP>The computed query cost is higher for a query-for-experts than for a query-for-cases.
When the query-for-experts is selected, returning the subset of experts is also based on an availability of the expert.
When the query-for-experts is selected, returning the subset of experts is also based on a rating of the expert.
When the query-for-experts is selected, returning the subset of experts is also based on a number of followers of the expert among users of the system.
When the query-for-experts is selected, the new case is provided to a selected one of the subset of experts for formulating a diagnosis.
The multidimensional representation of the medical case is computed based on a medical ontology.
The medical ontology may be based on the Unified Medical Language System.
The ontology includes parts of the human body.
The ontology includes biological functions.
The ontology includes medical conditions.
The ontology includes pharmacological substances.
A matrix of proximities is applied to the multidimensional representation of the new case to account for relationships between concepts in the ontology.
When the query-for-experts is selected, provision is made for making a payment to the expert for formulating the diagnosis.
The plurality of records may include laboratory test results.
The plurality of records may include images.
The plurality of records may include descriptions of symptoms.
The plurality of records may include results of patient monitors.
The plurality of records may include prescribed medications and treatments.
